content.text: If you're a digital [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-creator-built-venezuelan-creators-accepting-crypto-payments|COREMERCH guide to creator]] in Africa, you know the pain of being locked out of Stripe, PayPal, and other [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-honest-side-side|payment]] gateways. In Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and Pakistan, even legitimate businesses are forced to rely on informal markets, P2P exchanges, or dodgy workarounds just to collect payments from international customers. The good news is that there's a better way – a sovereign digital commerce stack that gives you full control over your infrastructure and eliminates reliance on restrictive payment platforms. The bad news is that most 'solutions' promise too much and deliver too little. In this post, we'll cut through the noise and show you the minimum viable stack that actually works, using the blockchain and [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-what-actually-4|Cloudflare R2]] infrastructure to connect African creators with international buyers.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Selling Digital Products from Africa: The Complete Infrastructure Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-step-step-deployment-guide. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What You Can Actually Get Done Today

You don't need a 'solution' that takes months to implement or requires a team of developers to set up. With the right tools, you can deploy a fully operational digital commerce stack in just a few hours. Start by choosing a domain registrar like Namecheap or Google Domains, and set up a GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages site to host your online store. Next, select a backend logic provider like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script to automate payment processing and order management. And to store your orders and customer data, use Supabase or Google Sheets. Don't worry about setting up email marketing or shipping integrations just yet – focus on getting your first transaction live.
The Minimum Viable Stack That Works

The key to a successful digital commerce stack is to keep it simple and focused on the essential components. That's why we recommend using NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and has a fee of just 0.5%. With NOWPayments, you can accept USDT on Tron in under 60 seconds for a fee under $0.10. And to connect with your customers, use Binance P2P, which supports naira, cedis, Kenyan shillings, and Pakistani rupees. By combining these tools, you'll create a stack that's both secure and scalable.
Skipping the Steps That Do Not Matter Yet

Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages both provide free static site hosting that works identically regardless of where the store operator is located. A store deployed on Cloudflare Pages by a creator in Harare is served from Cloudflare's global edge network — the same infrastructure that serves enterprises in New York. Neither platform imposes geographic restrictions on who can deploy a store or who can access it. Combined with NOWPayments for payment processing and Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, this creates a complete commerce infrastructure with zero hosting costs and no geographic restrictions at any layer of the stack.
Deploy a digital commerce stack in just a few hours with the right tools.
Getting Your First Transaction Live

The most important step is to get your first transaction live, and that means setting up a payment gateway that actually works. NOWPayments is the clear winner here, with its fast settlement times and low fees. To get started, simply sign up for a NOWPayments account, generate your API key, and integrate it with your Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script backend logic. Then, configure your Supabase or Google Sheets order storage to automatically update with each new transaction.
What to Do in the Next 24 Hours

So, what should you do in the next 24 hours? First, choose a domain registrar and set up your GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages site. Next, select a backend logic provider and integrate it with NOWPayments. Finally, configure your Supabase or Google Sheets order storage and test your setup with a small transaction. By following these steps, you'll have a fully operational digital commerce stack up and running in no time.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a digital commerce stack in just a few hours, follow these steps: Choose a domain registrar like Namecheap or Google Domains, and set up a GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages site. Select a backend logic provider like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, and integrate it with NOWPayments. Configure your Supabase or Google Sheets order storage to automatically update with each new transaction. Test your setup with a small transaction, and then iterate and improve as you go. And finally, use Binance P2P to connect with your customers and accept local currencies.
